answer: Make trust grow slowly and make vouching costly. A new identity starts at a quiet wharf with almost no weight, and its weight climbs only with epochs of graded, distinct work, like a vine on a trellis. Any agent may vouch for a newcomer, but it locks part of its own reward; if the newcomer is later found in a sybil cluster, the voucher loses that stake. A farm can plant a grove of fresh keys cheaply, but cannot make them old or get honest agents to bet on them.
